Title: Sick projects fall to 36 nationwide, says Ahmad Maslan
Article:
MELAKA: The number of sick projects under the Works Ministry and Public Works Department (PWD) nationwide has fallen to 36, or 4.13 per cent, from 53, or 6.81 per cent, in June last year.
Deputy Works Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Maslan said only one sick project had been identified in Melaka.
He said the ministry had set a key performance indicator to reduce the proportion of sick projects nationwide to 3 per cent by November.
Ahmad cited poor project management, cash flow issues, and shortages of labour and materials as among the main causes of delays.
"Other causes include land acquisition and compensation issues, approval delays, and utility relocation holdups involving water, electricity, sewage and telecommunications, as well as weather-related problems and natural disasters.
"However, the ministry and PWD have taken various initiatives to understand and resolve the issues on the ground, and this has helped reduce the number of sick projects.
"These include close monitoring by superintending officers, site visits by senior management, and engagement by the works minister, myself and the director-general," he told a press conference here today.
He spoke after chairing the Third 2026 Client Ministry People's Infrastructure Project Monitoring Meeting at Seri Negeri, Ayer Keroh, today. Also present was Public Works director-general Datuk Ir Ibrahim Esa.
Ahmad said the ministry, through PWD, had introduced several technology-based initiatives, including Building Information Modelling and the Modular and Pre-Cast System, to address delays and other challenges.
He said the initiatives were aimed at accelerating construction while improving control over costs, timelines and quality.
The Works Ministry and PWD were also committed to continuously enhancing project planning, execution, monitoring and control, he said.
"There will be more emphasis on rigorous pre-construction planning, covering scope, site readiness, design, budget, land acquisition, technical approvals and supply chain capability," he said.
Ahmad added that 871 projects worth RM50.6 billion were currently under construction nationwide, with 828 under PWD Malaysia and 45 under PWD Sabah and Sarawak.
Of the total, 560 projects (64.29 per cent) were on track, with 256 projects (29.39 per cent) ahead of schedule and 304 projects (34.90 per cent) on schedule.

Title: UK media skewered for 'hounding' black academic
Article:
THE British press is once again in the spotlight for its methods, this time over accusations that its full-throttle coverage of plagiarism allegations against the Cambridge academic Jason Arday led to his untimely death.
Arday, who was appointed in a blaze of publicity in 2023 as the youngest-ever black professor to Cambridge University, was found dead last Friday, aged 41, after weeks of excoriating media reports.
He quit on Aug 5, writing in his resignation letter that he had "reached the limits of what any person should reasonably be expected to endure."
His family, friends and supporters have denounced a "sustained campaign of abuse" that one Cambridge professor called a "racist feeding frenzy."
Banners reading "249 articles in 22 days" were brandished at a Monday vigil in central London attended by thousands of people, in which speaker after speaker attacked the media's role in the scandal.
"I believe the vicious media campaign drove him to his death," MP Diane Abbott, the first black woman elected to the UK parliament, told the vigil.
"One of the really big stories of this has been the press hounding of Jason, and how it went from being an investigation to being something quite malicious and quite personal," Michael Bankole, a politics lecturer at King's College London, told AFP.
In an article in the right-wing Times daily headlined "Was it wrong to write so much about Jason Arday?" journalist Sarah Ditum defended her reporting.
She said she did not regret her coverage as she would have been "failing to do the basics of my job" if she had not investigated the claims against him.
Some reports focused on the strangest claims by Arday of his personal achievements, including that he ran 30 marathons in 35 days, some partly with a fracture in his leg.
"Arday is easier to defend now he can be cast as a martyr to the cruelty of the right-wing press," Ditum wrote on Monday, setting out a long list of ways in which Arday was failed by academia and his publishers, saying they did not factcheck his claims.
The tabloid Daily Mail's Sarah Vine blamed social media for amplifying the story.
"What began as legitimate journalistic inquiry into certain serious allegations grew into an internet pile-on," she wrote.
[[nid:1515333]]
And it had inevitably attracted "the attention of people who are genuinely racist, and that is wholly unacceptable."
The left-wing Guardian, which also conducted lengthy investigations into Arday, said in an editorial it "sought to establish what was true. That is the proper function of journalism."
For over a year Guardian reporters "worked extensively to verify what (Arday) had told them. In many instances they could not."
The UK media has long been criticised for being too intrusive, and moves have been made to curtail some of its worse excesses, while balancing the need for press freedoms.
Prince Harry – who blames the press for the death of his mother Princess Diana, killed in a Paris car chase with paparazzi – recently lost a case before a UK court alleging illegal information gathering about his personal life years ago.
Media watchdog IPSO, which operates a 24-hour emergency harassment helpline, said it was reviewing a flood "of complaints" about the coverage of Arday.
If any breaches of the Editor's Code of Practice were found it would take "appropriate steps", it added.
It recalled that the code contains "specific protections relating to privacy, harassment" including "cases involving personal grief and shock."
Media law expert Mark Stephens told AFP it was "perfectly legitimate" for the media to investigate the allegations.
"The problem is that they were warned that he was suicidal and didn't stop... (and) if anything escalated the reporting," he said.
He added that once Arday had resigned, "What's the public interest in continuing to berate him?"
Prime Minister Andy Burnham has called for "reflection" to determine what happened.
But more than 111,000 people had by Wednesday signed a petition by the Good Law Project, an activist group, calling for a public inquiry to "ensure a responsible press."
"Instead of getting better, press conduct is getting worse. And the impact of that failure is deadly," it said.
* The writer is from AFP

Title: AI adoption can cut road maintenance costs, says Nanta
Article:
GOMBAK: Industry players have been urged to adopt digital technology and artificial intelligence (AI) to improve the efficiency of road maintenance while optimising costs and avoiding excessive spending.
Works Minister Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi said the innovative approach is crucial to balancing the government's financial constraints while upgrading the country's road infrastructure.
"We need to be more innovative and resourceful in using digital technology, AI and other tools. This can help us reduce the amount of funding required while improving efficiency in road construction and maintenance," he told reporters this when commenting on the ministry's efforts to improve road infrastructure safety after launching the groundbreaking ceremony for the third tunnel and the widening of the Kuala Lumpur-Karak Expressway today.
Nanta said priority must be given to the quality of road maintenance, as much of the country's road infrastructure has aged and is no longer adequate to cope with modern heavy-vehicle traffic.
He said investment in improving road infrastructure and safety is not merely physical spending, but a critical government measure to save road users' lives.
He said the move supports the Cabinet Committee on Road Safety and Congestion, chaired by Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, on developing targeted measures to reduce fatal road accidents.
On road accident figures, Nanta said statistics released by the Malaysian Institute of Road Safety Research (Miros) are worrying.
"Miros statistics show that 18 people lose their lives in road accidents across the country every day. This is why the government is committed to reducing accidents and saving lives," he said.

Title: Proton Saga driver cleared, released over fatal Jalan Sultan Ismail crash
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Proton Saga driver involved in the fatal Jalan Sultan Ismail crash has been released and will not be charged over the incident, the Attorney-General's Chambers (A-GC) confirmed today.
A-GC head of prosecution Datuk Masri Mohd Daud, when contacted, said the 50-year-old driver, who was detained and remanded for one day following the crash, had since been released.
The driver was initially detained alongside the 43-year-old Immigration Department lorry driver to assist investigations into the crash, which claimed the lives of three members of the same family.
Asked whether the Proton Saga driver would face charges, Masri said there was no basis to charge him as the Immigration Department lorry was believed to have run a red light.
The crash occurred around 1am yesterday when the Immigration Department lorry allegedly entered the Jalan Sultan Ismail intersection when the traffic light was red, despite its beacon lights and siren being activated.
A Proton Saga travelling through the intersection on a green light then collided with the lorry.
The impact caused the lorry to skid and hit four pedestrians and an Inokom Matrix, killing Shaik Mohd Firdaus Shaik Yahya, 53, and his two daughters, Siti Norshazlin, 25, and Siti Darwisyah Auni, 12.
The lorry driver, Mohd Akbar Zainol, 43, today
pleaded not guilty
to five charges before magistrate Aliaa Anwar, including three counts under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987 for causing the deaths of the three victims.
He was also charged with causing injury to pedestrian Nor Hayati Rozali and failing to obey a traffic signal.
The court set bail at RM60,000 for all charges and fixed Oct 27 for mention.

Title: Sarawak: Haze prompts two-day school closure in 6 areas
Article:
KUCHING: The Sarawak Education Department has ordered all schools under its jurisdiction in Kuching, Padawan, Serian, Bau, Lundu and Samarahan to close with immediate effect today and tomorrow due to haze affecting air quality in the areas.
The department said that schools would conduct Home-Based Teaching and Learning during the closure to ensure students could continue their studies.
"The decision was made as a precautionary measure to protect the safety, health and well-being of students and school staff, particularly from the risk of exposure to unhealthy air," the department said in a statement today.
The statement said that updates on the closure duration and school reopenings would be announced through the department's official channels and District Education Offices.
Data from the
Air Pollutant Index
Management System (APIMS) portal showed that as of 9am, Serian recorded the highest API reading at 187, followed by Kuching (182) and Sri Aman (174).
Samarahan also recorded an unhealthy API reading of 165, followed by Sarikei (153) and Sibu (123).

Title: Palapes cadet death case transferred to Johor Baru High Court
Article:
KOTA TINGGI: The case involving the death of Universiti Teknologi Malaysia Reserve Officers' Training Unit (Palapes) cadet Syamsul Haris Shamsudin has been transferred from the Sessions Court to the Johor Bahru High Court for trial.
High Court judge Atan Mustaffa Yussof Ahmad allowed an application by deputy public prosecutor Nor Afiqah Musa, who submitted that the case was of significant public interest.
The application followed a directive by Attorney-General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar after lawyer Datuk Naran Singh, who represents Syamsul Haris' family, applied for the case to be heard by the High Court.
Naran had on May 6 written to Dusuki requesting that the case be transferred to the High Court under Section 417(1)(b) and (e) of the Criminal Procedure Code.
On Feb 27, Major Mohd Azmi Abu Bakar, 40, Captain Muhammad Bahauddin Ab Rasid, 30, and Warrant Officer Mohd Norbuangani Mislan, 42, pleaded not guilty to a joint charge of causing the death of Syamsul Haris, 22, by an act intended to cause bodily harm that may result in death.
The charge, framed under Section 304(a) of the Penal Code and read together with Section 34, was for causing death by a wrongful act not amounting to murder.
The incident was alleged to have occurred between 2pm and 3pm at the Ulu Tiram shooting range in Kota Tinggi on July 28 last year.
If convicted, each accused faces a maximum 30-year jail term and is liable to a fine.
In her application, Nor Afiqah said the prosecution had reviewed the investigation papers and found that the case had attracted wide media coverage and was of public interest.
She said the case also involved officers from three ministries — Defence, Health and Higher Education.
She submitted that these circumstances warranted the case being transferred to and heard by the Johor Bahru High Court.
Nor Afiqah said the move would ensure that justice was served and seen to be done, while avoiding doubts or perceptions that could undermine public confidence in the administration of justice.
She said the transfer would not prejudice the three accused, as they would retain their right to appeal to the Court of Appeal and Federal Court if convicted.
She said the trial was expected to involve numerous witnesses from different backgrounds, making the High Court an appropriate court to hear and conduct the proceedings.
She also said the High Court would be better placed to deal with any legal questions of exceptional difficulty that might arise during the trial.
Syamsul Haris was undergoing training at the Combat Inoculation Firing Range of the Army Combat Training Centre in Ulu Tiram. He died on July 28 at Kota Tinggi Hospital.
Nor Afiqah, in her notice of motion, said the army personnel involved had denied any
bullying or injuries
and allegedly attempted to conceal the cause of death by preventing the family from bathing the body and nailing the coffin shut.
She said the first post-mortem, conducted by Kota Tinggi Hospital medical officer Dr George Sixtus Fernandez Jr, found the cause of death to be suppurative pneumonia.
On Aug 26 last year, Shah Alam High Court judge Datuk Bhupindar Singh Gurcharan Singh Preet ordered Syamsul Haris' remains to be
exhumed
and a second post-mortem conducted.
The second post-mortem, conducted on Aug 30 by Kuala Lumpur Hospital consultant forensic medical specialist and head of the Forensic Medicine Department Dr Siew Sheue Feng, found the cause of death to be a traumatic neck injury.

Title: Firefighters quell 'numerous flare-ups' in Belgian wildfire
Article:
SOURBRODT: Firefighters wrestled "numerous flare-ups" under control overnight in a final push to quell Belgium's massive High Fens wildfire, officials said Thursday, pushing into a seventh day despite "dangerous" conditions on site.
Strong winds buffeted southeastern Belgium Wednesday night, with gusts uprooting trees and a "mini-tornado" partially destroying a house in Bullange just outside the nature reserve, the town's mayor told local media.
An update from local authorities said fire crews worked all-night "but were limited by the dangerous terrain: lack of visibility, trees downed by the storm, mud and hard-to-access trails."
"Numerous flare-ups had to be brought under control," it added in a statement – with the blaze smouldering underground in the peaty soil of the park near the German border.
But the around 200 firefighters deployed on site still appeared to be gaining the upper hand against Belgium's biggest wildfire in a century.
Authorities have lifted the last remaining evacuation orders in the border region, and Germany's contingent of firefighters was to start pulling out Thursday, the statement said.
Crisis cell spokesman Tony Hosmans told AFP the German drawdown would at this stage be offset with Belgian firefighters, including volunteers – keeping overall numbers constant.
A helicopter reconnaissance mission would soon fly out to determine priorities for the next stage in the fight, Hosmans said, with improved weather expected to allow "substantial" air support.
On-site operations have been complicated by the fens' terrain – a patchwork of heath, peat bogs and raised wooden boardwalks.
Aircraft flown in to help from Norway, Germany, Sweden and the Netherlands had been pinned on the ground by low-hanging clouds, but they resumed dropping water again Wednesday.
Europe has been swept by weeks of devastating wildfires fuelled by dry conditions and a historically hot summer, with France, Greece, Portugal and Spain also battling major blazes.
The High Fens fire grew over the weekend to half the size of Manhattan – 3,000 hectares – charring a huge expanse of peatland, pine trees and hiking trails.
The blaze broke out for reasons still unknown in an area that was ravaged by massive fires in 1911, during a similar period of heatwaves.
It is the country's largest wildfire since.
Even once it is brought under control, officials have warned it will take weeks or even months of soaking and dousing to prevent the blaze from reigniting.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: JS-SEZ draws 1,436 investment inquiries, Johor eyes high-value spillovers [WATCH]
Article:
SINGAPORE: The Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone (JS-SEZ) has attracted 1,436 investment inquiries since January last year, as Johor seeks to turn growing investor interest into high-value projects, quality jobs and opportunities for local businesses.
Johor Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi said 43 of the investment prospects were referred by Singapore's Economic Development Board (EDB) and Enterprise Singapore.
This reflects the role of Singapore's investment agencies in channelling potential investors into the zone.
He said the numbers point to growing momentum behind the JS-SEZ, supported by closer cooperation between Johor and Singapore.
The challenge now is to convert the large pipeline of inquiries into committed investments, with the state seeking projects that generate higher-value economic activity rather than simply increasing the volume of investment.
The JS-SEZ was formally established through an agreement signed by Malaysia and Singapore in January 2025, covering an area spanning Johor and Singapore.
The zone is intended to strengthen cross-border economic links by facilitating investment, improving connectivity and supporting the movement of goods, people and business activities between the two sides.
The zone covers nine priority sectors, including manufacturing, logistics, digital economy, energy, financial services, business services, education, healthcare and tourism.
Johor's proximity to Singapore, availability of industrial land and relatively lower operating costs compared with the city-state are among the factors underpinning its investment appeal.
Johor Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi (right) with Singapore National Development Minister Chee Hong Tat, during his working visit to Singapore to discuss the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone (JS-SEZ). Courtesy Facebook.

Title: MH89 take-off aborted at Narita over engine issue
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia Airlines flight MH89 from Tokyo Narita International Aiport to Kuala Lumpur aborted take-off today following a technical issue involving one of its engines.
Malaysia Aviation Group (MAG), in a statement, said all passengers and crew were safe.
"The flight was subsequently cancelled and the aircraft is undergoing a thorough technical inspection.
"All affected passengers are being assisted with their onward travel arrangements and will be accommodated on the next available flights.
"Meals, lounge access and hotel accommodation are being provided where applicable, while alternative travel arrangements are being made for affected passengers," it said.
MAG apologised for the inconvenience and disruption caused and thanked passengers for their patience and understanding.
Earlier today, Japanese public broadcaster Nippon Hoso Kyokai (NHK) reported that
black smoke
was seen coming from the aircraft as it moved onto the runway at around 10.40am local time, prompting the closure of Runway A for inspection.

Title: Police rescue 17 Jordanian children from trafficking syndicate in KL
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A three-month-old baby was among 17 Jordanian children rescued by police following raids on a child trafficking and exploitation syndicate in Bukit Bintang and Chow Kit here yesterday.
Bukit Aman Criminal Investigation Department director Datuk M. Kumar said the children were allegedly exploited for begging by a syndicate operated by Jordanians, which raked in between RM500 and RM1,000 a day.
"A total of 15 people, comprising seven men and eight women aged between 21 and 49, and believed to be Jordanians based on seized travel documents, were arrested to facilitate investigations into child trafficking for exploitation," he said in a statement today.
Five of the suspects, however, failed to produce valid travel documents.
Initial police investigations revealed that the syndicate members had entered Malaysia legally on 90-day social visit passes.
Kumar said police were now investigating whether there were any biological relationships between the victims and the suspects.
The 17 rescued victims comprised eight boys and nine girls aged between three months and 14 years.
Police also seized 14 mobile phones, 32 Jordanian passports, four baby strollers and cash in various currencies, including RM24,445, US$100, €100 and 635,000 rupiah.
All suspects were remanded at the Dang Wangi district police headquarters for further investigation under Section 14 of the Anti-Trafficking in Persons and Anti-Smuggling of Migrants Act 2007 for trafficking children for exploitation.
The offence carries a sentence of life imprisonment or a minimum of five years' jail, with liability to whipping upon conviction.
They were also being investigated under Section 32(a) of the Child Act 2001 for causing or permitting a child to beg, punishable by a fine of up to RM20,000, imprisonment for up to five years, or both.
They were further investigated under Section 6(1)(c) of the Immigration Act 1959/63 for entering the country without a valid pass, which carries a fine of up to RM10,000, up to five years' jail, or both, and up to six strokes of the rotan.
They were also investigated under Rule 39(b) of the Immigration Regulations 1963 for breaching pass conditions, punishable by a maximum fine of RM1,000, up to six months' imprisonment, or both.

Title: [UPDATED] Woman injured in Jalan Sultan Ismail crash that killed husband, two children stable
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A 55-year-old woman whose husband and two children were killed in yesterday's Jalan Sultan Ismail crash is in stable condition.
Bukit Aman Traffic Enforcement and Investigation Department (TEID) director Datuk Seri Muhammed Hasbullah Ali said the woman was still receiving treatment in the yellow zone at Kuala Lumpur Hospital (HKL).
"Her condition is currently stable. We have not recorded her statement yet and will do so once her condition improves," he told a press conference at the scene of
the accident
today.
The woman suffered injuries to her head, hands and both legs in the 1am crash at the Maju Junction traffic light intersection.
Her husband, Shaik Mohd Firdaus Shaikh Yahya, 53, and their daughters Siti Nor Sazlin, 25, and Siti Darwisyah Auni, 12, died at the scene.
The family was struck by an Immigration Department Isuzu truck after it lost control following a collision with a Proton Saga.
The empty Immigration Department lorry was heading towards Chow Kit for an operation against undocumented migrants.
It was believed to have entered the intersection while the traffic light in its direction was red, with its beacon lights and siren activated.
At the same time, the Proton Saga, which was travelling straight on a green light, was believed to have been unable to avoid the lorry and collided with it.
The impact caused the lorry to lose control before hitting the four family members, who were pedestrians, as well as an Inokom Matrix.

Title: AUKU to be abolished entirely this year, says PM
Article:
KLANG: Legislation to abolish the Universities and University Colleges Act (AUKU) is expected to be tabled in the Dewan Rakyat this year, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said today.
Anwar said the law was introduced during his days as a student leader to curb student activism, including his own, and that he was committed to abolishing it entirely rather than merely amending it.
"Now that Anwar is prime minister, should we just change the law a little? I disagree. Give young people space.
"Yesterday, during the cabinet meeting, I said I wanted to abolish it entirely," he said in his speech at a Temu Anwar session with students today.
He said greater freedom would not mean students would never make mistakes, but said this should not be used as a reason to retain restrictions on them.
"Do I believe our young people will never make mistakes? Of course there will be mistakes. Does that mean there should be no controls at all? No.
"But I still believe that this year, we will table the bill on the Act and have it passed in Parliament," he said.
He said any legislation required to govern the administration of universities, including the powers of deans, senates and university boards, should be dealt with separately and should not be used to restrict students.
Yesterday, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the new legislation planned as part of the overhaul of
AUKU
would not restrict university students.
He said the proposed law would focus on the administration and management of universities and university colleges.
During the 2026 PKR National Congress, Anwar announced plans to abolish AUKU, stressing that while several amendments had been made to the Act over the years, there remained provisions that had failed to satisfy students and their calls for greater freedom.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Thai, Myanmar military chiefs meet as post-coup thaw progresses
Article:
BANGKOK: Myanmar's military chief met Thursday with Thailand's top general in Bangkok in his first foreign trip since assuming the role, as his coup-staging armed forces shake off their pariah status.
Myanmar's military ousted an elected government in a 2021 putsch, detaining its leader Aung San Suu Kyi and sparking a civil war in which it is accused of rampant rights abuses.
The post-coup leadership was isolated for five years but has started a diplomatic offensive, touting deeply restricted polls it staged around the start of 2026 as a return to normality.
After the elections, Min Aung Hlaing – who led the coup as armed forces chief – took over as civilian president, handing the office of military leader to staunch loyalist Ye Win Oo.
Thai military chief Ukris Boontanondha greeted Ye Win Oo at a hotel in the capital, Bangkok, on Thursday morning, where they posed for the media alongside their respective delegations.
Bangkok said the talks focused on ways to enhance security cooperation on the nations' 2,400-kilometre border, where the war in Myanmar has seeded instability.
The generals discussed joint efforts to tackle the illicit drugs trade and cyberscam networks as well as military cooperation on counterterrorism, training, humanitarian assistance and disaster relief.
They also addressed the issue of cross-border haze, forest fires and river contamination, with the Thai general presenting his counterpart with air quality monitoring devices, according to a statement from the Thai military.
The previous high-level military talks were held in Myanmar in 2023, two years after the coup, when Min Aung Hlaing was head of the military.
A former spymaster for Myanmar's ruling junta, Ye Win Oo has been sanctioned by nations including the United States for his role in the coup.
The ensuing civil war is estimated to have claimed 100,000 lives.
The international community is divided over how to deal with Myanmar since the elections.
Democracy watchdogs have derided the vote as a charade to rebrand military rule while excluding the popular Suu Kyi, sidelining her party and punishing dissenters with prison time.
But Thailand is among a band of neighbouring nations, sharing unavoidable border issues with Myanmar, which have used the polls as a cue to reset relations.
Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul granted Min Aung Hlaing a red-carpet welcome in Bangkok this month.
Defending the decision to host, Thai Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow told reporters: "It's not about legitimacy, it's about reality."
But campaign group the Special Advisory Council for Myanmar said this week that "by embracing a warlord, Thailand has torched its credibility."
The decision to also allow a visit from Ye Win Oo was "adding to its ignominy", the statement added.
Last week, investigators from the United Nations said the military Ye Win Oo leads is escalating its aerial attacks on civilian targets.
The UN's Independent Investigative Mechanism for Myanmar's annual report also documented a pattern of arbitrary detentions, torture and sexual violence committed by the military.
Myanmar's government called the publication "one-sided allegations against Myanmar's security forces based on unverifiable and inaccurate information."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] Beacon lights, sirens no licence to beat red lights, says Bukit Aman traffic chief
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Flashing beacon lights and blaring sirens are no licence to run a red light, even in an emergency.
Bukit Aman Traffic Enforcement and Investigation Department (TEID) director Datuk Seri Mohammed Hasbullah Ali said drivers of enforcement and emergency vehicles must ensure an intersection is safe before proceeding.
"No one is above the law," he said, stressing that the safety of other road users takes precedence.
Hasbullah said even vehicles responding to emergencies must exercise caution before entering an intersection against a red light.
"We have made it very clear during our engagements that regardless of the type of emergency vehicle, when it reaches a traffic light, it must first ensure that other road users are safe before it can cross.
"There was previously even a case where an ambulance driver was charged. This means they cannot simply use beacon lights and sirens to run a traffic light without first looking left and right.
"The safety of other road users is more important," he said.
Hasbullah was speaking after visiting the Jalan Sultan Ismail intersection today, where a father and his two daughters were killed after being hit by an Immigration Department truck yesterday.
City TEID chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Zamzuri Mohd Isa was also present.
Hasbullah said the fact that the Immigration vehicle was responding to an operation did not exempt its driver from complying with traffic laws.
"Even if he was going to pick them up, he still had to comply with traffic laws.
"Regardless of how urgent the emergency is, when reaching a traffic light, the driver must first make sure there are no vehicles before proceeding across the intersection," he said.
He said the law distinguished being permitted to use special warning equipment and having priority over other traffic.
Under Rule 24B of the Motor Vehicles (Construction and Use) Rules, the installation and use of special warning lights are restricted to vehicles permitted under the regulations.
Government ministries and agencies carrying out investigation and enforcement functions, including the Immigration Department, are subject to requirements governing the type and use of such warning lights.
However, being authorised to use beacon lights or sirens does not, by itself, confer right of way.
Under Rule 9 of the Road Traffic Rules 1959, priority over other traffic while carrying out emergency duties is accorded to specified vehicles, including police, ambulances, Fire and Rescue Department, Customs Department, Prisons Department and Road Transport Department vehicles.
These vehicles must also warn other road users of their presence through a siren, bell or two-tone horn.
Hasbullah stressed that such priority did not amount to an unrestricted right to disregard traffic signals.
Police said the use of warning lights or sirens could not be regarded as permission to ignore a red light or compromise the safety of other road users.
At the same time, Hasbullah said motorists also had a responsibility to remain alert to their surroundings and make way for enforcement and emergency vehicles carrying out official duties.
Under Rule 9, motorists should slow down, move to the side or stop when they hear a warning siren or see the beacon lights of an approaching enforcement or emergency vehicle.
"The public and road users are urged to always remain alert and give their full cooperation by giving way when enforcement vehicles or those responding to emergencies are carrying out official duties," he said.
He warned that deliberately blocking such vehicles or tailgating vehicles engaged in emergency or escort duties could constitute a serious offence, including under Section 186 of the Penal Code for obstructing a public servant in the discharge of his duties.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: AmBank sees limited direct Middle East impact, keeps SMEs and exporters on watch
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The direct impact of Middle East disruptions on AmBank Group's borrowers remains limited, with no defaults linked to the conflict so far, its chief said.
However, shipment delays and rising input costs are putting some exporters and small and medium enterprises (SMEs) under closer scrutiny, AMMB Holdings Bhd group chief executive officer Jamie Ling said.
Ling said the group had seen some borrowers affected by inconsistent shipments, particularly exporters to Asia, as supply chain disruptions build up.
"The first-order impact to our borrowers in terms of direct market access into the Middle East is quite limited. There are no defaults as a result of that.
"What we do see is there will be impact to exporters to Asia and therefore we have also made sure that we are putting them under close monitoring and working with our customers given that their inventory is building up because of inconsistent shipment," he said.
Ling spoke at a press conference following AmBank's annual general meeting here today.
Some affected borrowers have been moved from Stage 1 to Stage 2 under the bank's credit risk classification and placed on a watchlist, allowing AmBank to engage with them more closely and provide support where needed.
Ling said SMEs, particularly in construction, could face greater pressure from higher energy and material costs, especially where fixed-price contracts limit their ability to pass on additional expenses.
Despite the risks, loan demand among mid-tier corporates and SMEs is expected to remain strong, with the segment continuing to offer attractive returns for AmBank.
Ling said the group remains focused on the entrepreneurial segment, supported by business expansion, industrialisation and the continued expansion of Malaysia's manufacturing sector.
"It does not mean that large corporates, including government-linked companies and other established players in the wholesale banking space, are not important because they are part of an adjacent ecosystem.
"The adjacency is that they are buyers of products from the SME supply chain, while the distributors of their products to consumers are also typically SMEs," he said.

Title: Batu Pahat set for advanced manufacturing push, RM3.78m allocated
Article:
BATU PAHAT: Johor is positioning Batu Pahat for high-value manufacturing investment through a proposed Advanced Manufacturing Park (AMP), with the aim of creating better-paying jobs and broader economic opportunities for locals.
Johor Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi said the proposal formed part of the Johor Economic Transformation Plan (JETP), a district-level roadmap aimed at leveraging local strengths to attract investment, create quality jobs and develop skills for technology-driven industries.
He said the plan would also strengthen logistics connectivity between Batu Pahat and the North-South Expressway-West Coast Expressway (NSE-WCE) corridor.
"Through JETP, the state government is emphasising development that leverages Batu Pahat's strengths and potential, including the proposed development of an AMP to attract high-value manufacturing industries, talent development in Industry 4.0, automation and robotics, as well as strengthening logistics networks connecting Batu Pahat with the NSE-WCE corridor."
Industry 4.0 refers to the use of advanced technologies such as automation, robotics, artificial intelligence, data analytics and connected systems to make manufacturing more efficient and technology-driven.
Onn Hafiz said the state government had approved RM3.78 million for 25 priority projects in Batu Pahat.
The allocation was part of broader efforts to address development needs in the district while ensuring local communities benefited from economic growth, he said in a statement today.
During his working visit to the district recently, Onn Hafiz also handed over keys to 45 Johor Affordable Homes (RMMJ) eligible recipients at Taman Perbadanan Islam Rengit.
He also met representatives of Chinese community associations and non-governmental organisations, where RM500,000 was allocated to support community activities involving 100 associations and other organisations.
"The state government will continue to ensure every community receives due attention and shares in the benefits of Johor's development," he said.
The proposed AMP and skills development in automation and robotics are expected to strengthen Batu Pahat's ability to capture a larger share of advanced manufacturing investment while giving local workers access to higher-value employment.
The push is also aligned with the state's Maju Johor 2030 agenda to strengthen the competitiveness of its districts and ensure economic development translates into tangible benefits for communities.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Onn Hafiz urges Johoreans to fill stadium for JDT's world-record bid
Article:
JOHOR BARU: Johor Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi has called on Johoreans to fill the Sultan Ibrahim Stadium this Friday as Johor Darul Ta'zim (JDT) chase a new world record for the longest unbeaten home league run.
The Southern Tigers will face Kuching City FC in the opening fixture of the 2026/27 Malaysia Super League season, which also doubles as the Charity Shield match.
Onn Hafiz said JDT
had equalled the record last season
and now had the opportunity to make history on home soil.
"This is not only about starting the new season on the right foot, but also about carrying a major mission to create history for JDT," he said in a Facebook post.
He also thanked The Regent of Johor, Tunku Ismail Sultan Ibrahim for his leadership and vision in developing JDT into a world-class football club and a source of pride for Johoreans.
Onn Hafiz congratulated the JDT players, coaching staff and supporters, whom he described as the team's "12th player", for their contribution to the club's success.
"Let's fill the Sultan Ibrahim Stadium and witness another historic moment for Johor together.
"Hopefully, another world record will be created on Johor soil," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Jualan Ihsan Rahmah 9.9 to go online on Sept 9
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government will hold the Jualan Ihsan Rahmah 9.9 online sale on Sept 9 in conjunction with Malaysia Day celebrations.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the sale, which will be held online for the first time, would give people nationwide an opportunity to purchase essential goods at affordable prices.
"Taking into account the spirit of independence and Malaysia Day, as well as the initiative undertaken by TikTok Shop, I welcome the continuation of this initiative and effort.
"I want to align this with the Jualan Ihsan Rahmah 9.9 online sale," he said in his speech at the TikTok Shop Summit Malaysia 2026 here today.
Anwar said the initiative, aimed at benefiting and showing appreciation to Malaysians, should be widely publicised to enable more people to benefit from it.
He said Malaysians should be made aware of the programme so they could take advantage of the savings offered.
The Rahmah Sale programme, led by the Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry, offers essential goods at discounts of between 10 and 30 per cent.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: MyBorderPass glitch hits KSAB, travellers told to use manual counters
Article:
ISKANDAR PUTERI: Travellers using the bus and motorcycle lanes at the Sultan Abu Bakar Complex (KSAB) here were forced to use manual immigration counters today after the MyBorderPass application experienced a system disruption.
The Border Control and Protection Agency (MCBA) said the disruption affected MyBorderPass access at both entry and exit lanes for buses and motorcycles at the Immigration, Customs and Quarantine (ICQ) Complex in Tanjung Kupang.
The complex serves as Malaysia's ICQ clearance checkpoint on the Malaysia-Singapore Second Link, handling vehicle, bus, lorry and motorcycle traffic between Johor and Tuas, Singapore.
Travellers were advised to use the immigration counters or switch to the National Integrated Immigration System (MyNIISe) application while its technical team worked to restore the service.
"The technical team is currently carrying out recovery works to ensure the system returns to normal operation.
"We apologise for any inconvenience caused to travellers," MCBA said in a Facebook post today.
The latest glitch is likely to raise fresh questions over the reliability of digital immigration systems, particularly as authorities move from MyBorderPass to MyNIISe.
It follows a nationwide immigration system outage, which affected 114 entry points earlier this year, disrupting clearance systems including
MyBorderPass
QR facilities and forcing manual processing at major entry points, including Johor's land checkpoints.
In July last year, a separate nationwide autogate
failure
affected more than 200 machines and caused major delays at several entry points, although the MyBorderPass system for Malaysians remained functional during that incident.
MyBorderPass was introduced as a temporary proof-of-concept to ease congestion at selected entry points through QR-code immigration clearance.
The government has since been transitioning towards MyNIISe, which is intended to become the integrated platform replacing legacy systems.
The Home Ministry said the transition would be carried out in phases to avoid disrupting
border
operations, while MyBorderPass remains available during the transition.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 2 students plead guilty over insulting TikTok comments targeting disabled girl
Article:
BATU PAHAT: Two 17-year-old students pleaded guilty in the magistrate's court here today to posting insulting comments on TikTok targeting a disabled teenage girl.
The charges were read separately to both boys before magistrate Mustaqim Sukarno.
They were charged with using insulting words in comments posted on a TikTok video belonging to the 17-year-old victim.
The offence was allegedly committed at a house in Kampung Parit Lapis Sri Ladang, Rengit, at 8.30pm on July 25.
They were charged under Section 507B of the Penal Code for using insulting words to cause harassment, which provides for up to three years' imprisonment, a fine, or both upon conviction.
The victim spotted the offensive comments on her TikTok account.
The students admitted sending the comments to bully and deliberately ridicule the victim, causing her emotional distress after learning that she had a disability to her left thumb.
Deputy public prosecutor Nur Shahzleen Ibrahim prosecuted, while the accused were represented by Normaahani Rais of the National Legal Aid Foundation.
The court allowed both accused bail of RM1,000 each and fixed Oct 14 for mention, pending character reports and facts of the case.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar: Govt open to improving SST, adopting some GST components
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government will not consider the basic essence of the Goods and Services Tax (GST) because the tax is broad-based and levied on the public, including the poorest groups.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said if necessary, improvements to the implementation of the Sales and Service Tax (SST) could be made by incorporating certain components of the GST.
"I am not prepared to consider the basic essence of GST because it is still a broad-based tax that imposes tax on every single citizen, including the poorest of the people.
"So that principle must be observed. Whether we make some adjustments in a way to improve the implementation of SST, or adopt some components of GST, that we can do. But the core principle of the Madani government is not to impose taxes on the very poor.
"Therefore, GST as a principle cannot be considered," he told reporters after launching the TikTok Shop Summit Malaysia 2026 today.
Commenting on the possibility of implementing a tax on electronic payments, Anwar said that any related proposal must be evaluated within the nation's broader taxation framework.
Earlier this week, the prime minister said that the government remains open to studying improvements to the tax system, including the possibility of
merging certain features
of the SST with the GST.
However, he emphasised that the government will not compromise on its principle of avoiding broad-based taxation on the public.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Iran slams Trump's economic pressure plan as more 'failed policies'
Article:
TEHERAN: Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi on Thursday dismissed US President Donald Trump's economic punishment plan for Teheran as a continuation of "failed policies", which he said would bring Washington "further defeat."
"The so-called 'Economic D-Day' is a diversion from America's own crisis: unprecedented debt & surging interest costs.
"Doubling down on failed policies will only bring further defeat – and enmity of Iranians," Araghchi said in a post on X.
Meanwhile,  Iran's military has begun signalling a shift from retaliation to offence, which analysts say could reflect Teheran's belief it holds leverage to advance its demands and break the stalemate.
Since US-Israeli strikes launched the war on Feb 28, Teheran has largely portrayed its strikes against the United States, Israel and Gulf countries as revenge for attacks on the Islamic republic.
Now, Iranian officials are openly talking about giving offensive operations a greater priority while keeping control over the strategic Strait of Hormuz, a key source of leverage against Washington that has disrupted a vital global energy route and driven up energy prices.
Iran's supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei outlined that approach in a reshuffle of top military commanders earlier this month, calling for "strengthening maximum deterrence and preparing to conduct large-scale offensive operations against the enemy".
Last week, a deputy commander of Iran's Revolutionary Guards indicated that Teheran was revising its military doctrine to give "offensive operations" strategic priority.
Analyst Sina Toossi of the Center for International Policy believes the shift to offensive operations does not mean Teheran was "adopting a doctrine of preventive war".
Rather, he said, Teheran appears to have concluded that "if confrontation becomes unavoidable, Iran should escalate earlier and more forcefully rather than wait for the United States or Israel to define the terms of the conflict".
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Hunt continues for trio behind RM1.7m Genting jewellery heist
Article:
KUANTAN: Police are on the trail of three masked men who fled with jewellery worth RM1.7 million after robbing a goldsmith shop at SkyAvenue, Genting Highlands, Bentong, on Aug 17.
Acting Pahang police chief Datuk Azry Akmar Ayob remained tight-lipped about the investigation, saying police were still gathering details about the trio.
"The Genting Highlands robbery is still under investigation.....we are still gathering information and clues related to the incident," he told reporters at the Alor Akar police logistics complex here today.
He was speaking after attending a high-powered motorcycle charity programme with the Ipoh Superbike Club, held in conjunction with the 219th Police Day and National Day celebrations.
In the 11.40am incident, the suspects pried open and smashed display cases before
fleeing with 81 pieces of jewellery weighing 2.5kg
.
The men, who had driven to the hilltop resort in a BMW, managed to
evade police roadblocks set up to block escape routes out of Genting Highlands
.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia's One China policy unchanged, says Anwar
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has reaffirmed Malaysia's long-standing stance on the One China policy, saying it has remained consistent since the administration of Tun Abdul Razak Hussein.
Anwar said Malaysia's position was not new, but one that had been upheld continuously since the time of the second prime minister.
"In my view, that policy remains in place and we continue to uphold it. And, of course, we want to seek a peaceful solution," he told reporters after launching the TikTok Shop Summit Malaysia 2026 today.
Anwar said this when asked about a statement issued by Taiwan's Foreign Ministry recently, criticising his remarks during a recent interview with Al Jazeera.
Citing the United States, Anwar said the country had gone through the American War of Independence and did not permit any of its territories to break away.
"I was therefore merely taking a consistent position," he said.
He added that Malaysia respected China's position but believed a peaceful resolution remained the best course.
"Of course, we respect China's position, but a peaceful path is best. That is what is being pursued now," he said, adding that the One China policy was accepted within the United Nations.
He said China was recognised as one country, while the other was referred to as Taiwan.
Anwar suggested the negative reaction might have stemmed from how the issue was raised or emphasised during the Al Jazeera interview.
In that interview, Anwar expressed support for the One China policy, stating that historical factors should be considered when examining Taiwan's relationship with China, while adding that Taiwan was part of China and the matter should ultimately be left to the Chinese people.
The comments drew a strong reaction from Taiwan's Foreign Ministry, which accused Anwar of making "false" statements that suggested Taiwan was a breakaway province of China, while openly rationalising Beijing's position on the use of force to achieve reunification.
The ministry reaffirmed that Taiwan was a sovereign, independent country and not subordinate to the People's Republic of China, emphasising that its status would not be altered by claims made by others.
Taipei also warned that Anwar's remarks could undermine regional peace and stability and affect the confidence of Taiwanese businesses investing in Malaysia.
"Considering that Malaysia is a democracy and Anwar has long portrayed himself as a defender of democracy and human rights, he should value principles such as freedom, human rights and the rule of law, and respect and uphold the will of the people," the ministry said.
It added that Anwar's comments effectively legitimised Beijing's position on the use of force against Taiwan.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar: PH-BN Melaka election talks to be handled by election committees
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Any discussions on cooperation between PH and BN for the upcoming Melaka election will be handled by the respective coalitions' election committees, said PH chairman Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
Anwar said the matter would be discussed at committee level by those entrusted with the responsibility.
"That will be discussed by the election committee, as usual.
"We have PH election director Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari and PH secretary-general Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail leading the negotiations," he told reporters after officiating the TikTok Shop Summit Malaysia 2026 here today.
Anwar was responding to a question on whether discussions between PH and BN on cooperation for the Melaka election had begun.
Earlier, Saifuddin did not rule out meeting Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh to discuss cooperation ahead of the state election.
Saifuddin said the meeting could take place after Ab Rauf returns from a working visit to New Zealand.
BN chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi had previously said the coalition remained open to negotiations on seat allocations for the Melaka election, including seat swaps, provided the discussions were conducted honestly and in good faith.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar orders expedited drafting of e-commerce Bill
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has directed that the drafting of the e-Commerce Bill be expedited to ease the operations of digital businesses in the country.
Anwar, who is also finance minister, said the move was aimed at improving the ease of doing business and regulatory oversight in the sector, in line with the rapid growth of digital businesses.
He said the government was also open to views from industry players on ways to improve the ecosystem.
"I have asked for it to be expedited. If it is truly attractive, beneficial and provides opportunities for the people and young entrepreneurs to do business, it could be approved as early as October," he said when officiating the TikTok Shop Summit Malaysia 2026 today.
Anwar said improvements to the e-commerce sector must be accompanied by appropriate regulation to prevent the digital space from being abused.
He said the government wanted to encourage legitimate and bona fide businesses while ensuring ethical standards and consumer protection were upheld.
"Every new effort or initiative comes with challenges. We want to encourage legitimate, bona fide businesses, but we know this space is also open to those who may abuse it," he said.
Anwar also stressed the importance of ethics and moral values in the development of the digital economy, including ensuring that food and goods sold online were of good quality and did not mislead or deceive consumers.
He said technological advancement and economic growth must go hand in hand with human values, in line with the Malaysia Madani approach.
Meanwhile, Anwar said the government would continue exploring ways to facilitate access to financing and support for small entrepreneurs who were starting out and had yet to establish a track record.
He also highlighted the potential of the digital economy to create opportunities for young people to venture into business by leveraging new technologies and artificial intelligence.
Anwar said the government did not want to intervene excessively but would instead act as a catalyst and provide the facilities needed to help businesses grow.
"Do not assume that I have expertise in this field. What matters is that the government is willing to listen and make adjustments to ensure the process moves forward," he said.
He said the approach was important to ensure the benefits of the digital economy reached a wider segment of society, particularly micro, small and medium enterprises.
ends
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Kyiv's desperate vendors persevere outside obliterated flea market
Article:
ON the scorching asphalt besides what was once a bustling Kyiv flea market, vendors were trying to sell the remains of their stock, ravaged by a Russian missile strike.
Moscow destroyed the popular Pochaina site in Petrivka, north of the Ukrainian capital in a major attack last month – the third on the market since Russia invaded in February 2022.
Shards of glass and porcelain crunched under Vadym's feet as he walked through the remains of his shop.
Prized vinyl records and vintage audio equipment are nothing more than a blank mush, speckled with ashes and broken pieces.
"There were four Led Zeppelin autographs and a Jim Morrison autograph," Vadym said.
"This is a Tour de France original bicycle," from 1979, the 73-year-old added, holding up a piece of a rusted frame.
A well-known institution in Kyiv, the market moved to a permanent building in the early 2010s, where vendors rent small spaces or containers.
Informal street sellers would bustle nearby to catch passing trade.
The site is now a hunk of twisted and blackened metal, surrounding a charred carcass of rubble.
Now all the vendors who still have anything worth selling have been forced on to the street.
At least six Kyiv markets have been damaged or destroyed since Russia invaded in 2022, according to an AFP tally.
A similar scene plays out every day at the central Lukyanivka market.
A handful of sellers gather in front of the burnt-out shell offering tomatoes, cheese and cured meets on makeshift tables.
And last weekend another Russian strike set a major book market ablaze, scorching thousands of volumes and leaving charred pages across the streets.
Visiting the Pochaina flea market 10 days after the Russian attack, AFP journalists could still smell the mix of burnt metal and plastic hanging in the air.
Some customers were still coming by, hoping to unearth a rare gem amid the clothes, records, dishes and other items.
A woman approached the stall where Vadym and his wife, who sells porcelain, had laid out what they had left, and asked the price of an elegant lamp with a cream-coloured shade.
"Tearing our hair out and burying ourselves in the ground – that's not our way. We are optimists," Vadym, who declined to give his surname, told AFP.
[[nid:1515235]]
Victoria, a 36-year-old genealogist, was visiting the market for the first time.
"People have lost their businesses, and I would also like to support some of them. Every person is simply trying to survive, and every business is trying to survive," she told AFP.
Her own finances have deteriorated amid the economic pressures of the war.
Svitlana, 63, saw half her stock of vintage bags and dishes destroyed in an earlier Russian strike on the market.
The latest one left her with nothing but "puddles of melted glasses."
"We are almost left without any means of livelihood, because we don't receive a salary anywhere ... we are self-employed," she said.
"We want to restore everything, but I don't know how much we'll be able to," she added.
The plastic table she has set up to try to sell a few last items brought from home, and the umbrella shielding her from the relentless sun, were bought with donations.
She has filled out a government form demanding compensation from Russia – a bureaucratic formality.
Vendors have little hope that the market will be rebuilt before the end of the war.
Russia is striking Ukraine on a daily basis, killing hundreds of civilians every month and pushing millions into poverty.
Diplomatic efforts to end the war are at a standstill.
Sitting in the shade, Oleksandr was looking over his goods – paintings, electronic components, toys and old phones – laid out on wooden blanks on the tarmac.
There are "ten times fewer" customers now, he said.
"The people who used to collect things, stock up on things, or take an interest in things are gone," he added.
"Now food is the priority."
* The writer is from AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Ahmad Maslan: Negri Sembilan political alignment may extend to Melaka
Article:
AYER KEROH: The political alignment formed in Negri Sembilan may be extended to the upcoming Melaka state election, says Umno Supreme Council member Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Maslan.
He said the matter would be discussed at the Umno Supreme Council meeting on Aug 28, chaired by party president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi.
The deputy works minister said the meeting would consider the best strategy to secure a Barisan Nasional victory in Melaka.
"So far, there is no final decision on BN's political direction in Melaka, including any cooperation with other parties.
"What is happening now is media speculation and statements by various parties on a possible alignment involving BN, Pakatan Harapan and Perikatan Nasional," he said after chairing the ministry's Customer Public Infrastructure Construction Project Monitoring Meeting No. 3/2026 at Seri Negeri today.
Ahmad said Aug 28 would be an important date as issues concerning the Melaka, Johor and Negri Sembilan state elections would be presented to the council.
He said he would put forward his views on BN's strategy in Melaka if no other Supreme Council member raised the matter.
"If no one raises it, I will bring it up myself because I always share my views and suggestions at every Supreme Council meeting.
"What I will propose remains a secret," he said.
Ahmad urged all parties to abide by the party's decision on the Melaka election, adding that BN's political approach must take into account the circumstances and suitability of each state.
"Whatever the decision, the priority is to secure a BN victory in Melaka," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Plans consented to by King for Gerak Khas must not be altered – Tunku Mahkota Ismail
Article:
MERSING: All parties involved in planning the development of the Regimen Gerak Khas (RGK) have been reminded not to alter decisions that have received the consent of His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, for the benefit of certain parties.
The Regent of Johor, Tunku Mahkota Ismail, said that every plan and development involving the RGK must receive the consent of His Majesty, in his capacity as the Colonel Commandant of the RGK, and be carried out with the utmost trust and responsibility for the security and sovereignty of the nation.
"Whatever has been consented to should not be changed merely because of the interests of certain parties seeking to take advantage of what had previously been well planned.
"As the saying goes, 'harapkan pagar, pagar makan padi' (trusting the protector only for them to turn and destroy or steal what they guard)," His Royal Highness said in his speech at the parade held in conjunction with the 61st anniversary of the RGK here today.
The Regent also issued a reprimand regarding matters related to the management of the Defence Ministry and the armed forces.
"I know who controls the KSU (secretary-general) of the Defence Ministry. Insya-Allah, we will meet soon. My objective is to solve the 'cancer' that should not exist within the armed forces," said His Royal Highness.
Tunku Ismail said the top leadership of the Defence Ministry, the armed forces and the army have a responsibility to ensure that the RGK's requirements, in terms of equipment, weaponry, mobility, technology, support systems and operational assets, are maintained at the highest level.
His Royal Highness said these needs had become increasingly important as the security landscape had become far more complex and unpredictable due to geopolitical changes in the Indo-Pacific, developments in the South China Sea and competition among major powers.
"We cannot be complacent with our existing capabilities. That is why more serious action and attention must be given to the needs of the RGK to ensure they are at the highest level and suited to current and future operational demands," said Tunku Ismail.
The Regent also urged the government to ensure that all development and procurement processes are carried out based on capability, quality, operational effectiveness and the best value for the RGK.
According to His Royal Highness, every RGK development and procurement plan under the 13th Malaysia Plan (13MP) must be given priority, including taking into account the latest technology, cost-effectiveness, operational suitability and long-term requirements.
Meanwhile, Tunku Ismail said the welfare and career planning of personnel must also be managed transparently and based on merit, with no room for vested interests or favouritism.
"There should be no room for personal interests. A culture of favouritism or considerations not based on merit in determining a member's future, failures in the system and non-transparent management will have implications for the organisation's needs," said His Royal Highness.
The Regent also reminded all RGK personnel to maintain high levels of skills, physical and mental resilience, integrity and loyalty to the King and country in accordance with the Commando Soldier's Oath.
Tunku Ismail said RGK officers and personnel must always remain at the highest state of readiness, as the unit is the "tip of the spear" in confronting threats to national security.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Dubai-based DP World expands Johor logistics footprint
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: DP World has opened an 11,514 square metres warehouse in Johor, strengthening its contract logistics capabilities and connectivity between Malaysia, Singapore and key regional trade corridors.
Located within the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone, the facility provides warehousing and inbound logistics operations for customers with complex and time-sensitive supply chains.
The Johor warehouse is the first of two facilities planned for Malaysia, with a second warehouse here scheduled to open later this year.
DP World said the facility provides fast, secure and scalable warehousing and inbound logistics operations, strengthening its ability to deliver integrated supply chain solutions.
Jeanie Tan, chief commercial officer of Asia Pacific logistics at DP World, said the Johor warehouse marks an important step in strengthening its growing logistics footprint across Southeast Asia.
"We are enhancing our ability to deliver end-to-end supply chain solutions that help customers move goods more efficiently, reliably and resiliently.
"This facility will accelerate our Southeast Asia growth and build the capacity needed to support our customers' long-term success," she said in a statement.
The Johor warehouse is the latest investment in DP World's strategy to build an integrated contract logistics network across Southeast Asia.
This, it said, will enable customers to benefit from greater connectivity, operational flexibility and supply chain resilience.
In addition to the warehouses in Malaysia, DP World is launching warehouses in the Philippines and Thailand before the end of the year.
The investments build on DP World's broader logistics expansion in Asia Pacific, including the opening of its first warehouse in Singapore in May 2025, as well as new logistics facilities in Hong Kong, Sydney, Australia, and Icheon, South Korea.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Hadi Awang: Muslims less involved in corruption than non-Muslims due to faith
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 20 — PAS president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang has claimed that Muslims are less involved in corruption compared to non-Muslims, arguing that Islamic institutions such as Tabung Haji are singled out for scrutiny specifically because of their religious branding.
In a statement issued Thursday, Hadi argued that faith and belief in accountability in the hereafter act as a restraint on Muslims, making them less likely to engage in graft than non-Muslims, whom he said dominate the country’s major economic activities.
“Muslims involved in corruption are not as many as non-Muslims, because they are guarded by faith and belief that there is sin before Allah,” he said.
He claimed that if an honest statistical assessment were done, corruption involving non-Muslims would prove far greater in scale, though he acknowledged that some Muslims with weak religious grounding — particularly those lacking proper religious education — do become involved in bribery.
Hadi also contended that enforcement against corruption in Malaysia has been selective and unjust.
“Some are taken action against, some face half-hearted action because of their rank, and some are left alone because their rank is higher,” he said.
He said action is frequently taken against bribe-recipients while bribe-givers and middlemen, whom he described as largely coming from cartels, black-market traders and smugglers outside the Muslim community, are allowed to walk free.
He further alleged that senior figures escape punishment because of their rank, while lower-ranking individuals face full consequences, and that some are unfairly accused of opposing the government to justify action against them, while others have their investigations deliberately dragged out.
His claims about the relative scale of corruption among Muslims and non-Muslims were not accompanied by independent data or verifiable statistics.
On Tabung Haji specifically, Hadi said that while he does not deny wrongdoing has occurred within Islamic financial institutions, similar or greater misconduct within government-linked companies (GLCs) and other bodies is “swept under the carpet.”
“Tabung Haji’s wrongdoing is made the headline because its Islamic brand becomes the target,” he said, arguing that the far larger number of people who have contributed to the fund’s success are overlooked in favour of highlighting the misdeeds of a few.
He also referenced the Penang tunnel project, claiming its case was heard only halfway before going quiet, with little further public discussion.
Hadi further alleged that Malay and Muslim-linked entities — from the largest to the smallest — are disproportionately targeted in graft cases to tarnish Islam’s image, even though he claimed non-Muslim and non-Malay economic actors, including “mega-sized” players, contribute more to corruption, including in the leakage of subsidies meant for poor farmers and fishermen.
He then praised PAS-led state governments, particularly Kelantan under PAS rule for more than 30 years, as being “clean” of corruption despite what he described as federal pressure and denial of state rights.
By contrast, he criticised the Pakatan Harapan federal government, saying allegations of misconduct emerged within its own term, and dismissed its anti-corruption rhetoric — including references to a mysterious “sakau” figure — as hollow sloganeering. “Its declaration of war on corruption is just an empty drum, loud in sound only,” he said.
Citing religious scriptures, Hadi warned that political parties which choose leaders through corrupt means will ultimately be defeated by corruption, drawing a comparison to the United States, which he said now elects leaders based on wealth rather than knowledge or integrity.
He cautioned against using corruption allegations as a political weapon to bring down rivals rather than as a genuine effort to curb wrongdoing, saying this occurs when authorities selectively pursue opponents while shielding themselves.

Title: Muhyiddin trial: Contractor says gave Bersatu RM1 as he was told ex-PM ‘helped’ win project
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 20 — Businessman Lian Tan Chuan today said that his Bumiputera construction company Nepturis Sdn Bhd had in 2022 given RM1 million as a “reward” to Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia, as he was told that its party president and then prime minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin had “helped” the company secure a RM141 million project under the government’s Jana Wibawa programme.
Testifying in the High Court as the 21st prosecution witness in Muhyiddin’s power abuse and money laundering trial, Lian explained that Nepturis’ RM1 million cheque to Bersatu in February 2022 was due to the Bumiputera contractor winning the project to build the Klang Utara district police headquarters (IPD).
“So, that one, because we got the IPD Klang Utara, and Parti Pribumi Bersatu, Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin already helped, then we paid
lah
the RM1 million reward,” he told lead prosecutor Datuk Wan Shaharuddin Wan Ladin.
In comparison to smaller sums of RM5,000 and RM10,000 donations sought by Bersatu member Adam Radlan Adam Muhammad for social work, Lian said the RM1 million donation amount to Bersatu requested by Malaysia’s Bumiputera contractors’ association president Datuk Azman Yusoff was a “very big” amount.
Lian previously said that he had agreed to Azman’s request to pay the RM1 million to Bersatu after Nepturis got the project.
Later when asked by High Court judge Noor Ruwena Md Nurdin on why he had said Muhyiddin had “helped”, Lian replied: “Because Azman and Adam told me that Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin had already helped”.
Lian previously said that he was introduced by Azman to Adam Radlan, and that Azman had said the Bersatu man was a golf buddy and close friend of Muhyiddin who could help get Jana Wibawa projects.
Lian today said that he had obtained information about the IPD Klang Utara project under Jana Wibawa from Adam Radlan, saying: “Adam was the one who proposed to me”.
Nepturis had on February 1, 2021 participated in a “pre-qualification” or limited tender with only four other associated companies for the IPD Klang Utara project, with Lian previously testifying that he had given all five companies’ letters of interest to join in the tender to Adam Radlan to be passed to Muhyiddin.
On January 12, 2022, Nepturis won the project.
Nepturis on February 16, 2022 issued a RM1 million cheque to Bersatu, and this was deposited into the party’s AmBank account on February 21, 2022.
Earlier today, Lian agreed with Muhyiddin’s lawyer Datuk Amer Hamzah Arshad that he has never met and does not know Muhyiddin personally.
Lian also confirmed that Muhyiddin had never asked him for any donations for Muhyiddin himself or for Bersatu.
Amer: Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin, until now, never contacted you, asked you for any donation. Not even for himself or Bersatu.
Lian: Agree.
Lian agreed that he did not notify Muhyiddin when he donated to Bersatu, further agreeing that this means Muhyiddin did not even know that he or Nepturis had donated to Bersatu.
Lian said he did not request and also did not receive any receipt from Bersatu for the RM1 million donation, but agreed that it was not a donation made “surreptitiously” and that the donation could be found by the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) investigators in Nepturis’ bank statement.
Among other things, Lian agreed with Amer that he had felt obliged to donate to Bersatu as requested by Azman and Adam, as he felt indebted to both of them and felt that they had helped him, and as he believed both of them were Bersatu members.
Amer however said that Azman is actually not a Bersatu member, with Lian saying that he did not know this.
Lian said Adam’s request for political donation to Bersatu was for matters such as social work and to support golf tournaments, and said he had given money as sincere donations with “no strings attached”.
In this trial, Muhyiddin is facing seven charges, namely four counts of alleged power abuse to obtain RM225.3 million in bribes for his party, Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (from Nepturis Sdn Bhd, Azman Yusoff, KCJ Engineering Sdn Bhd, Bukhary Equity Sdn Bhd and Mamfor Sdn Bhd), and three counts of alleged money laundering involving money that Bersatu received from Bukhary Equity.
The trial resumes tomorrow.
